## Context

Certified unlearning [@guo2020certified; @sekhari2021remember] asks the output of
an unlearning algorithm $\U$ to be indistinguishable from *retraining from
scratch* on the retain set. Write $\mu \approx_{\varepsilon,\delta} \nu$ for
$(\varepsilon,\delta)$-indistinguishability of two output distributions.

::: {#def-classical name="certified unlearning (retraining reference)"}

For every $\D$ and every partition $\D = \Dr \sqcup \Df$,

$$
\U\bigl(\A(\D),\, \Dr,\, \Df\bigr) \;\approx_{\varepsilon,\delta}\; \A(\Dr).
$$ {#eq-classical}

:::

This is presented as the unlearning analogue of differential privacy
[@dwork2006calibrating]. It is not.

## Idea

> The retrained model is not the released model minus $z$. It is the released
> model minus $z$ **and** minus the unlearning procedure. Comparing against it
> charges that procedure gap to $z$'s privacy budget.

Fix a forget point $z \in \Df$ and name three distributions over released models:

$$
\underbrace{\U\bigl(\A(\D),\Dr,\Df\bigr)}_{P:\ \text{$z$ present}}
\qquad
\underbrace{\U\bigl(\A(\D\setminus z),\Dr,\Df\setminus z\bigr)}_{Q:\ \text{$z$ absent, same procedure}}
\qquad
\underbrace{\A(\Dr)}_{R:\ \text{$z$ absent, different procedure}}
$$ {#eq-three}

What the release says about $z$ is the $P$ / $Q$ gap: one mechanism, one record
moved. @eq-classical constrains the $P$ / $R$ gap instead, and $P$ and $R$
differ in two ways at once — by the record *and* by the procedure that produced
them. So any test separating $P$ from $R$ reports a mixture of two signals.

The second signal is the $Q$ / $R$ gap: how far *unlearning a dataset that never
contained $z$* is from *training on that same dataset from scratch*. It has
nothing to do with $z$. For any inexact $\U$ it is non-zero, and it does not
shrink as the leakage about $z$ shrinks — it is still there when there is
nothing at all to leak. This is a **bias of learning procedure**, not noise, and
it can push the answer either way.

Removing it costs one substitution: replace $R$ by $Q$, so the two worlds differ
by the record and nothing else.

::: {#def-rectified name="rectified certified unlearning"}

For every $\D$, every partition $\D = \Dr \sqcup \Df$, and every $z \in \Df$,

$$
\U\bigl(\A(\D),\, \Dr,\, \Df\bigr)
\;\approx_{\varepsilon,\delta}\;
\U\bigl(\A(\D \setminus z),\, \Dr,\, \Df \setminus z\bigr).
$$ {#eq-rectified}

:::

The same bias sits in the audits, and this is where the rectified definition
already has an empirical counterpart. U-LiRA and its descendants
[@hayes2024inexact] score unlearned models against *retrained* shadow models:
the measured ROC separates $P$ from $R$, so a record with no leakage at all
still scores whatever procedure gap the algorithm carries.
RULI [@naderloui2025ruli] is the framework that removes it. Its **Game 2** fixes
an adversary-chosen target set *before* unlearning and then asks whether a target
$z$ was trained-then-unlearned or never trained — both worlds releasing the same
$\U\circ\A$, only the presence of $z$ changing. That is exactly @eq-rectified,
with the procedure held fixed and the bias cancelled by construction.

The rest of this note situates @def-rectified against @def-classical, then asks
what it costs to write it as differential privacy.

## Formalisation

### Rectified versus classical

The two definitions are related, but the gap is exactly group privacy.

::: {#prp-sufficient name="the retraining model is a pivot"}

@def-classical at $(\varepsilon,\delta)$ implies @def-rectified at
$\bigl(2\varepsilon,\,(1+e^{\varepsilon})\delta\bigr)$.

:::

*Proof.* For $z \in \Df$, removing $z$ leaves the retain set untouched:
$(\D\setminus z)_r = \Dr$. So @def-classical applied to $\D$ and to $\D\setminus z$
bounds $(P,R)$ and $(Q,R)$ against the **same** $R$; conclude by the triangle
inequality. $\square$

Note what the second instance is: it asks $Q \approx R$, i.e. that unlearning a
$z$-free dataset be indistinguishable from training on it. @def-classical does
not correct the procedure bias — it forbids it outright. That is why it is
sufficient, and also why it asks more than protecting $z$ requires.

The pivot also exists only because $z$ is a forget point. For $z \in \Dr$ the
references are $\A(\Dr)$ and $\A(\Dr\setminus z)$ and @eq-classical says nothing
— protecting retain points is $\A$'s job.

::: {#prp-necessary name="converse, lossy"}

Assume the no-op axiom $\U(\theta,\Dr,\emptyset) = \theta$. Then @def-rectified
at $(\varepsilon,\delta)$ implies @def-classical at
$\bigl(k\varepsilon,\;\delta\,\tfrac{e^{k\varepsilon}-1}{e^{\varepsilon}-1}\bigr)$,
$k = |\Df|$.

:::

*Proof.* Peel the forget points off one at a time; after $k$ steps the state is
$\U(\A(\Dr),\Dr,\emptyset) = \A(\Dr)$. Constants are the standard group-privacy
degradation [@dwork2014algorithmic]. $\square$

So @def-classical is the group-level version of @def-rectified at group size
$|\Df|$: sufficient but wasteful, charging the whole forget-set budget for a
guarantee audited one record at a time. And the converse needs an axiom usually
left implicit — any $\U$ that unconditionally takes a gradient step or injects
noise violates it.

### The data space has to change

Now try to write @def-rectified as $M(D) \approx M(D\setminus z)$. The
obstruction is immediate: $\U\circ\A$ is not a function of a dataset. It takes
three arguments, and the partition $(\Dr,\Df)$ is an extra input channel — same
$\D$, different forget request, different output law. There is no mechanism on
$\mathcal{Z}^{*}$ to apply DP to.

Move the channel into the records. With
$\mathcal{Z} = \mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y}$, put

$$
\tilde{\mathcal{Z}} \;=\; \mathcal{X} \times \mathcal{Y} \times \{\mathsf{r},\mathsf{f}\},
$$ {#eq-augmented}

so an **unlearning-aware dataset** $\tilde\D \in \tilde{\mathcal{Z}}^{*}$ is data,
labels, *and* each record's retain/forget status. Writing $\pi,\pi_{\mathsf r},
\pi_{\mathsf f}$ for the three projections, the single randomised mechanism

$$
M(\tilde\D) \;=\; \U\bigl(\A(\pi\tilde\D),\, \pi_{\mathsf r}\tilde\D,\, \pi_{\mathsf f}\tilde\D\bigr)
$$ {#eq-mechanism}

*is* a mechanism on a dataset, and @def-rectified is literally
$M(\tilde\D) \approx_{\varepsilon,\delta} M(\tilde\D\setminus\tilde z)$ for
$\tilde z = (x,y,\mathsf{f})$.

### Two neighbourhoods, one asymmetry

On $\tilde{\mathcal{Z}}^{*}$ the removal-neighbourhood splits by status, and
nothing forces one budget on both:

$$
\tilde\D \sim_{\mathsf f} \tilde\D\setminus(x,y,\mathsf f),
\qquad
\tilde\D \sim_{\mathsf r} \tilde\D\setminus(x,y,\mathsf r).
$$ {#eq-neighbours}

Call $M$ $(\varepsilon_{\mathsf f},\varepsilon_{\mathsf r})$-private if it is
$\varepsilon_{\mathsf f}$- and $\varepsilon_{\mathsf r}$-indistinguishable across
the two. Then $\varepsilon_{\mathsf f}$ small with
$\varepsilon_{\mathsf r} = \infty$ is unlearning;
$\varepsilon_{\mathsf f} = \varepsilon_{\mathsf r}$ is differential privacy,
which is why a DP learner unlearns for free; and
$\varepsilon_{\mathsf f} \ll \varepsilon_{\mathsf r} < \infty$ is the regime
nobody states.

> Unlearning is not a weaker privacy notion. It is differential privacy on a
> typed data space with an **asymmetric budget** across record types.

The typing also rules out substitution neighbours. Allow the *relabelling*
neighbour $\tilde\D_{z:\mathsf r} \sim \tilde\D_{z:\mathsf f}$ — same $(x,y)$,
status flipped — and chain it with the forget guarantee:

$$
M(\tilde\D_{z:\mathsf r}) \;\approx\; M(\tilde\D_{z:\mathsf f}) \;\approx\; M(\tilde\D\setminus z).
$$

Keeping $z$ as a training point now looks like never having seen it: the two
budgets collapse into one and $\A$ learns nothing from $z$. So the status is the
one coordinate that must **not** be protected, and only removal neighbours make
sense here — unlike in DP, where removal and substitution are interchangeable up
to a factor of two.

## Open questions

- **Q1.** Is @prp-necessary tight? $\U$ processes all of $\Df$ in one call rather
  than $k$ adaptive steps, so a better-than-$k\varepsilon$ bound may exist for
  specific $\U$.
- **Q2.** Without the no-op axiom the chain of @prp-necessary never reaches
  $\A(\Dr)$, the procedure gap stays unconstrained, and the two definitions
  become incomparable. Which deployed $\U$ actually satisfy the axiom?
- **Q3.** Sequential requests are a composition on $\tilde{\mathcal{Z}}^{*}$ with
  an adaptively chosen status vector. Does the typed budget compose, and does the
  adaptivity failure of @chourasia2023forget survive the reformulation?
- **Q4.** RULI's shadow models already give the three populations of @eq-three,
  so the $Q$ / $R$ gap can be measured directly. On standard benchmarks, how much
  of the leakage reported by retrain-referenced audits is just procedure bias?
